skill.name: gsap-plugins
skill.description: Guidance for registering and configuring GSAP plugins for scrolling, layout transitions, dragging, text effects, SVG animation, easing, and physics.
skill.summary: Choose GSAP plugins and apply documented setup, animation patterns, accessibility options, and cleanup practices.
skill.author: greensock

content.value_statement: GSAP plugin selection and configuration can be difficult across scrolling, text, SVG, and drag interactions. This skill provides focused examples, option references, and lifecycle guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explain public package installation, plugin imports, and registration before first use.
Guide ScrollToPlugin scrolling and describe ScrollSmoother wrapper structure and dependencies.
Provide Flip layout transition patterns and Draggable interactions with InertiaPlugin momentum.
Explain SplitText splitting, accessibility settings, responsive re-splitting, cleanup, and ScrambleText effects.
Describe DrawSVG stroke reveals, MorphSVG shape transitions, and MotionPath alignment options.
Provide CustomEase and physics examples, plus guidance on development-only GSDevTools usage.
limitations: This skill is a Markdown reference, not an executable animation engine or automated test suite.
ScrollTrigger, core tweening, and detailed React integration are delegated to related skills.
Some plugins receive brief descriptions rather than complete setup examples.
Generated suggestions require installed dependencies, suitable DOM or SVG elements, and browser testing.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive Layouts
use_cases.description: Apply Flip transitions and constrained dragging with momentum to lists, grids, and panels.

use_cases.title: Create SVG Motion
use_cases.description: Choose stroke drawing, shape morphing, or path-following techniques and configure relevant plugin options.

use_cases.title: Review Animated Typography
use_cases.description: Check SplitText accessibility, font loading, responsive re-splitting, and cleanup before integrating animated headings.

prompt_templates.title: Register a Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to install GSAP, import ScrollToPlugin, and register it before scrolling to a section with a header offset.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plugin setup and a first scroll animation

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Layout Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Help animate a grid reorder with Flip. Explain when to capture state, change the DOM, and start the transition.

prompt_templates.title: Build Responsive Text Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SplitText line reveal using autoSplit and onSplit. Include accessibility settings, font loading considerations, and cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: responsive text and lifecycle handling

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Complex SVG Morph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MorphSVG configuration for twisted multi-segment paths. Compare shapeIndex, map, rotational interpolation, and precompile; identify version-dependent options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: SVG morph debugging and performance review

output_examples.input: My DrawSVG animation does not show anything.
output: Confirm the SVG element has a visible stroke and nonzero stroke width.
Register DrawSVGPlugin before creating the tween.
Check the initial and target visible stroke segments; DrawSVG changes strokes, not fills.

output_examples.input: My SplitText line animation breaks after resizing.
output: Enable autoSplit for line splitting and create the animation inside onSplit.
Return the tween or timeline so re-splitting can clean up and synchronize progress.
Restore the original markup when the component unmounts.

output_examples.input: Should I use Flip or Draggable for reordering cards?
output: Use Draggable for pointer-driven movement and Flip for transitions between layout states.
Capture the Flip state before changing the layout, then animate from that state.
Register InertiaPlugin if the drag interaction needs momentum after release.

best_practices: Register each plugin before first use and import it from the public gsap package.
Restore SplitText markup during cleanup and return animations from onSplit when using autoSplit.
Preserve text accessibility and keep GSDevTools out of production builds.
anti_patterns: Using a plugin before registering it with GSAP.
Configuring obsolete private registry tokens to access GSAP plugins.
Treating DrawSVG as a fill animation or omitting visible stroke styling.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides GSAP plugin examples, configuration references, and usage guidance for an AI coding assistant.

faq.question: Does it install GSAP automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents public package installation and imports; the skill itself contains no installation script.

faq.question: Do the instructions require an authentication token?
faq.answer: No. They direct users to the public gsap package and explicitly reject obsolete private registry token configuration.

faq.question: Does it cover ScrollTrigger in depth?
faq.answer: No. ScrollTrigger has a separate skill; this reference covers ScrollToPlugin and describes ScrollSmoother dependencies.

faq.question: Can it help with accessible text animation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains SplitText aria settings, nested semantic content considerations, re-splitting, and markup restoration.

faq.question: Are the examples tested in my application?
faq.answer: No. Verify plugin versions, imports, target elements, cleanup, and browser behavior in your project.
